q: משה בן 71 עם סוכרת סוג 2 מטופל באינסולין. השבוע היו לו 2 אפיזודות היפוגליקמיה עם תסמינים. איזה מהבאים נכון לגבי נהיגה?
o: יכול להמשיך לנהוג אם נושא גלוקוז ברכב
צריך להפסיק נהיגה זמנית עד לייצוב הסוכרת
יכול לנהוג רק נסיעות קצרות מתחת ל-30 דקות
נהיגה מותרת רק אחרי בדיקת סוכר לפני כל נסיעה
explanation:
היפוגליקמיה תסמינית עלולה לפגוע לפתע בריכוז, בתגובה ובהכרה בזמן נהיגה. יש לברר את הסיבה ולייצב את המצב. **צריך להפסיק נהיגה זמנית עד לייצוב הסוכרת**.

**א. יכול להמשיך לנהוג אם נושא גלוקוז ברכב.** נשיאת גלוקוז מועילה לטיפול אך אינה מונעת אירוע בהפתעה.
**ב. צריך להפסיק נהיגה זמנית עד לייצוב הסוכרת.** הפסקה זמנית נועדה למנוע סיכון עד לייצוב והערכה.
**ג. יכול לנהוג רק נסיעות קצרות מתחת ל-30 דקות.** גם נסיעה קצרה מספיקה להתרחשות היפוגליקמיה.
**ד. נהיגה מותרת רק אחרי בדיקת סוכר לפני כל נסיעה.** ערך תקין לפני הנסיעה אינו שולל נפילה בהמשך.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר מנכ״ל 6/2023, עמ׳ 3–4, סעיפים 7, 9–11.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 6/2023: הגדרה מחדש של חובת ההודעה על נהגים עם מצבי בריאות העלולים לסכן את עצמם וזולתם

q: קשישה בת 78 מאושפזת ביחידה לטיפול נמרץ. בתה שואלת על מצבה הרפואי ודורשת לדעת את כל הפרטים. למטופלת אין ייפוי כוח או הוראות מוקדמות. איך יש לנהוג?
o: למסור לבת את מלוא המידע מפני שקרבת משפחה מקנה גישה לרשומה
לבדוק תחילה אם המטופלת הסכימה למסירת מידע לבתה
למסור לבת מידע כללי ללא בירור הסכמה מפני שמידע כללי אינו סודי
לדרוש מהמשפחה ייפוי כוח כתנאי לקבלת הסכמה ישירה מן המטופלת
explanation:
סודיות רפואית חלה גם ביחסים עם בני משפחה. כשהמטופלת כשירה אפשר לשאול אותה ישירות למי מותר למסור איזה מידע. **לבדוק תחילה אם המטופלת הסכימה למסירת מידע לבתה**.

**א. למסור לבת את מלוא המידע מפני שקרבת משפחה מקנה גישה לרשומה.** קרבת משפחה אינה הרשאה למסירת כל הרשומה.
**ב. לבדוק תחילה אם המטופלת הסכימה למסירת מידע לבתה.** מבררים את העדפת המטופלת ואת היקף הסכמתה.
**ג. למסור לבת מידע כללי ללא בירור הסכמה מפני שמידע כללי אינו סודי.** גם מידע כללי על מצבה עשוי להיות מידע רפואי אישי.
**ד. לדרוש מהמשפחה ייפוי כוח כתנאי לקבלת הסכמה ישירה מן המטופלת.** הסכמה ישירה שלה אינה מחייבת ייפוי כוח.

אסמכתא · חוק זכויות החולה, סעיפים 19 ו־20, עמ׳ 18 ו־19.
ref: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 · PDF pp.18–19, sections 19–20

q: What does overflow fecal incontinence that resembles diarrhea represent, and what finding should guide its treatment?
o: Watery leakage around impacted stool, calling for clearance of the impaction
Watery leakage indicating an empty colon, calling for reduced laxative use
Watery leakage indicating rapid transit, calling for suppression of bowel movements
Watery leakage excluding stool retention, calling for deferral of rectal assessment
explanation:
Overflow incontinence allows liquid stool to leak around a retained mass. **Identify and clear fecal impaction** to treat the cause of apparent diarrhea.

**A. Clear retained stool.** Disimpaction removes the obstacle around which liquid stool leaks.
**B. Assume an empty colon.** Loose output can coexist with substantial retained stool.
**C. Suppress bowel movements.** Slowing transit can worsen impaction and perpetuate leakage.
**D. Defer rectal examination.** Digital examination can detect the distal fecal mass and guide treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1363, 1376.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 1363, 1376

q: A healthy 72-year-old man takes lisinopril for hypertension and exercises regularly. He asks whether supplements advertised as targeting aging pathways will help him live longer. What should guide your advice?
o: Recommend the supplement on the strength of its proposed biological mechanism
Defer supplement use pending rigorous clinical data and FDA review
Recommend the supplement on the strength of its over-the-counter availability
Recommend the supplement on the strength of claims from an unregulated clinic
explanation:
An aging-pathway effect in a laboratory cannot show whether a person lives longer or experiences harm. **Defer using this supplement for longevity until rigorous human evidence shows meaningful benefit and acceptable risk.** In the United States, dietary supplements generally are sold without FDA premarket approval for efficacy.

**A. Recommend from the mechanism.** A plausible pathway does not quantify survival benefit, adverse effects or interactions with lisinopril.
**B. Wait for clinical data and FDA review.** Waiting for outcome evidence is appropriate. A new drug seeking authorization for a therapeutic indication faces an approval process distinct from the rules for ordinary dietary supplements.
**C. Recommend because it is over the counter.** Availability establishes neither lifespan benefit nor safety in this patient.
**D. Rely on clinic claims.** Testimonials and marketing do not compare clinical outcomes or harms against an appropriate control.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 602–603. FDA, Information for Consumers on Using Dietary Supplements.
Key note: FDA does not approve ordinary dietary supplements for safety and efficacy before sale. The relevant reason to defer is lack of demonstrated clinical benefit, not an expected premarket supplement approval.

q: An 84-year-old woman who lives alone and manages her medications was independent in basic ADLs until three days ago. Her daughter finds her acutely confused and inattentive. Temperature is 37.1°C, heart rate 88/min, blood pressure 108/62 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 20/min. She is oriented to person only and repeatedly asks when her husband, who died two years ago, will arrive. Medications include donepezil 10 mg, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and zolpidem 10 mg nightly, started one week ago. Which interpretation should guide the initial assessment?
o: Progression of dementia; focus on the chronic cognitive trajectory
Delirium; review zolpidem and investigate other acute contributors
Primary depression; focus on mood before evaluating acute illness
Primary psychosis; focus on delusions before evaluating acute illness
explanation:
The tempo of a mental-status change matters more than the strangeness of a belief. Zolpidem is a newly introduced hypnotic that may impair attention.
**Recognize delirium, review zolpidem and examine for other acute contributors to the three-day change.**

**A. Progression of dementia; focus on the chronic cognitive trajectory.** Her previous independence and sudden loss of attention call for investigation beyond chronic cognitive decline.
**B. Delirium; review zolpidem and investigate other acute contributors.** The recent hypnotic is a modifiable exposure. Its timing does not exclude concurrent illness.
**C. Primary depression; focus on mood before evaluating acute illness.** A mood assessment may be relevant later, but it does not address abrupt inattention and disorientation.
**D. Primary psychosis; focus on delusions before evaluating acute illness.** Asking for her deceased husband is not sufficient evidence of primary psychosis in this acute medical context.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882–885

q: A 78-year-old man requires analgesia after hip-fracture surgery. The team wants to reduce opioid exposure while maintaining pain treatment. Which principle is consistent with enhanced recovery after surgery?
o: Rely on increasing the opioid dose as the central analgesic strategy
Postpone analgesic treatment to reduce exposure to medicines after surgery
Combine analgesic approaches while minimizing opioid use after surgery
Use one analgesic mechanism to reduce the range of postoperative medicines
explanation:
Enhanced recovery after surgery uses several analgesic mechanisms to support mobilization. **Combine appropriate nonopioid or regional treatments and reserve opioids for the amount of pain relief still needed.**

**A. Rely on increasing the opioid dose as the central analgesic strategy** Repeated opioid escalation increases sedation and respiratory risk.
**B. Postpone analgesic treatment to reduce exposure to medicines after surgery** Untreated postoperative pain hinders mobility and can contribute to persistent pain.
**C. Combine analgesic approaches while minimizing opioid use after surgery** Oral or IV acetaminophen and selected regional techniques illustrate how mechanisms can complement each other.
**D. Use one analgesic mechanism to reduce the range of postoperative medicines** Depending on one mechanism defeats the opioid-sparing purpose of the approach.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1055, 1061–1062.

q: A 79-year-old man with depression, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and chronic pain reports worsening mood and poor sleep six months after his wife's death. He drinks three to four glasses of wine nightly to sleep. He takes sertraline 100 mg daily, started four months ago, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, and diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime. His PHQ-9 score is 22. Which approach directly addresses the two sleep self-treatments that Hazzard identifies as problematic in older adults?
o: Continue diphenhydramine and increase the evening alcohol used for sleep.
Continue alcohol for sleep and increase the bedtime diphenhydramine dose.
Stop diphenhydramine for insomnia and address the alcohol used for sleep.
Continue both sleep self-treatments while changing the antidepressant.
explanation:
Alcohol disrupts sleep quality, and diphenhydramine adds prolonged sedation and anticholinergic effects. **Stop using diphenhydramine for sleep and address nightly alcohol use**, assessing dependence and withdrawal risk while also treating his severe depressive symptoms.

**A. Increase alcohol.** More evening alcohol can worsen fragmentation and compound sedative effects.
**B. Increase diphenhydramine.** Higher exposure can worsen next-day fogginess and urinary retention in a man with prostatic enlargement.
**C. Address both exposures.** Review alcohol safely and use a behavioral sleep plan alongside assessment of depression and bereavement.
**D. Change antidepressant alone.** Mood treatment matters but leaves both problematic sleep self-treatments in place.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 661.

q: A care-home resident with dementia and behavioral problems is assessed for possible pain. What was the first step in the empiric stepwise pain-treatment protocol described in Hazzard?
o: Begin an initial therapeutic trial of acetaminophen
Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an antipsychotic
Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an opioid
Wait for a detailed verbal description of the pain
explanation:
Unrecognized pain can appear as agitation in dementia. **Start the described stepwise empiric protocol with acetaminophen** and assess behavior and comfort.

**A. Acetaminophen trial.** A scheduled trial can reveal whether pain relief improves distress.
**B. Antipsychotic first.** Suppressing agitation does not treat a painful cause.
**C. Opioid first.** The protocol reserves escalation for inadequate initial analgesia, while severe acute pain warrants individual assessment.
**D. Wait for detailed self-report.** Use behavioral signs and caregiver observations when communication is impaired.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1048.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An older patient develops delirium after admission for myocardial infarction and coronary catheterization. Several medications were started together. Which approach to evaluating medication contributions follows Hazzard?
o: Review all medications and the timing of changes alongside the medical evaluation
Attribute delirium to the new antiplatelet drug and change it before reviewing medications
Attribute delirium to the new statin and reduce it before evaluating other causes
Attribute delirium to the new beta-blocker and replace it before the general examination
explanation:
When several medicines start together during a major illness, temporal association alone cannot identify the offending agent. Obtain a dose-by-dose exposure history and examine the patient.
**Review all prescribed and nonprescription drugs, their timing and the medical course following infarction and catheterization.**

**A. Review all medications and the timing of changes alongside the medical evaluation.** The comprehensive history permits comparison of competing causes and potential interactions.
**B. Attribute delirium to the new antiplatelet drug and change it before reviewing medications.** A recent antiplatelet drug needs its indication and risks reviewed before any change.
**C. Attribute delirium to the new statin and reduce it before evaluating other causes.** There is no finding singling out the statin over other newly introduced drugs or cardiac illness.
**D. Attribute delirium to the new beta-blocker and replace it before the general examination.** Replacing the beta-blocker on timing alone could neglect ongoing cardiac or respiratory abnormalities.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882, 885

q: איזה מהשינויים הפיזיולוגיים מתרחש בלב המזדקן?
o: תאי קיצוב ב-AV NODE יורדים בשיעור של מעל 90% עם כניסת שומן במקומו
הקרדיומיוציטים קטנים והופכים רגישים יותר לסטרס מכני
הזדקנות מעלה יכולת של ה-SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM לצבור ולשמור סידן
פיברוזיס דיפוזי נצפה במיוקרדיום לאור הצטברות של קולגן אינטרסטיציאלי
explanation:
The aging myocardium becomes stiffer and relaxes more slowly. **Interstitial collagen accumulation produces diffuse myocardial fibrosis**, contributing to impaired diastolic filling.

**A. AV-node pacemaker loss.** Prominent pacemaker cell loss concerns the sinoatrial node. AV nodal tissue can develop fibrosis.
**B. Smaller cardiomyocytes.** Surviving myocytes commonly enlarge as other cells are lost.
**C. More calcium retention.** Sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium reuptake declines, slowing relaxation.
**D. Interstitial fibrosis.** Collagen deposition reduces ventricular compliance.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1116-1117.

q: בת 95 עם ממצא מקרי של פרפור עליות. נשקלת האפשרות לטיפול בנוגד קרישה. איזה מהבאים מהווה רכיב ב- HAS-BLED Score?
o: אי ספיקת לב
דיברטיקולוזיס
יתר לחץ דם
עבר של חבלת ראש
keySource: IMA 2025-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q142
ref: Official reference (book not stated) · ch. 77 · p. 1207 · Table 77-7
explanation:
HAS-BLED estimates bleeding risk during anticoagulation and identifies modifiable factors. **Uncontrolled hypertension is a scored component**, conventionally systolic pressure above 160 mm Hg.

**A. Heart failure.** It contributes to stroke-risk assessment, not a separate HAS-BLED point.
**B. Diverticulosis.** Diverticulosis alone does not count as a prior major bleed.
**C. Hypertension.** Poorly controlled systolic pressure increases bleeding risk and is potentially modifiable.
**D. Prior head injury.** Trauma alone is not the same as documented bleeding or stroke.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1202.

q: מה מהממצאים הבאים אופייני לתסמונת Takotsubo ?
o: ירידה במוטיליות הקיר הקדמי של הלב באקו לב
הרמות ST באק"ג
רמות תקינות של טרופונין בדם
חסימה של כלי דם בצנתור
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 316 – Cardiogenic Shock and Pulmonary Edema
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q109
explanation:
Takotsubo syndrome causes transient regional ventricular dysfunction and can resemble acute MI. **ST elevation is a recognized acute finding.** A typical apical pattern involves multiple apical or midventricular segments and usually extends beyond the territory of a single coronary artery.

**A. Reduced anterior-wall motion.** Anterior segments can be hypokinetic as part of apical ballooning. This finding in isolation is nonspecific, and the option does not describe the broader distribution that distinguishes the syndrome.
**B. ST elevation.** Evaluate urgently for acute coronary occlusion because the ECG appearance can overlap.
**C. Normal troponin.** Troponin commonly rises, though the degree of elevation is often modest relative to the ventricular dysfunction.
**D. Obstruction on angiography.** A culprit occlusion explaining the full wall-motion pattern suggests MI. Coronary disease can nevertheless coexist with Takotsubo.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2019, 2331. International Expert Consensus Document on Takotsubo Syndrome, Part I, 2018.
